title: Bua:
headline: Who picks Watsi's patients? People like Bua, who lived the same need.
story: A 20-second short from Mackinnon's “How do patients get chosen?” answer. Only the Bua passage. Bua was born during the war in Burma. She fled to Thailand as a refugee. Today she helps families on that same border get care.

One person, one story, said straight to camera. The last line is the whole video: “She's not visiting the need. She lived it.” Hopeful and proud, not sad. Do not repeat the V03 FAQ: no question card from V03, no process, no stats.
do: Open on frame 1 with the question as top text. No fade, no logo.
Keep Mackinnon's natural pauses. Do not tighten every gap.
Make the name super big. First name only, after the top text leaves.
Hold 1 second on her face after “She lived it.”
Caption the name as Bua. Never put Bua in a name super.
dont: No Medellín patient B-roll over the Bua lines. Those are not Bua's families.
No music, no slow motion, no sad tone.
No title card or logo at 0:00.

transcript:
Mincho5145.MP4 (Mackinnon, FAQ “How do patients get chosen?”). Times are mm:ss in the source file. The transcript writes Watsi as WOTC.
--- Mincho5145.MP4 ---
[00:00] Okay, so how do patients get chosen?
[00:06] People often ask me how our patients are chosen.
[00:08] How could I possibly sit at my desk on the other side of the world and know who has the
[00:13] highest need?
[00:14] Well, this really comes down to our trusted medical partners and how interwoven they are
[00:19] in their own communities.
[00:21] These are hospitals, clinics, organizations we've worked with for years and vetted closely.
[00:26] A nurse or a social worker flags a patient who needs surgery and can't pay for it.
[00:31] And these reps are from the community.
[00:33] One of them, Bua, from our medical partner in Burma, was born during the war there.
[00:39] She had to flee to Thailand as a refugee with her sisters, and today she is the person that's
[00:43] helping families along that same border get care.
[00:46] She's not visiting the need.
[00:48] She lived it.
[00:49] Our local reps get consent from the family, collect information, take photos, write up
[00:53] a brief story.
[00:54] Then it comes to us.
[00:55] We review it, we verify it, and we post the story on wotc.org.
[00:59] We don't choose based on who's the most compelling story or the most photogenic.
[01:04] We post patients as they come in and for those who have the highest need.
[01:08] There's hundreds of people waiting for care who haven't been shared yet.
[01:12] And every time you fund a patient, you're helping make sure we can show up for the next
[01:16] person in need too.
